solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An attack stops female having kittens

indicators.note: a stopper fills a gap, so the attack is plugged with the female letter

parts.note: taken as written
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: An assault halts a cat that is giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having kittens' is British slang for being very anxious, not giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a panicky, nervous state is frightened.

clue.text: Pacifist admires negotiated end to war

indicators.note: something negotiated is worked out and rearranged, so the letters are reordered
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A peace-lover admires a negotiated end to conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes away weapons from others favours peace, as a pacifist does.

clue.text: 6, not 18, applications to collect little book

indicators.note: to collect is to take in, so the pieces gather the book inside them
18 down means nasty; its synonym 'awful' is a familiar anagram signal

parts.note: uses are applications
Heb is the abbreviation for Hebrews, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A comedy that is not dreadful, with apps that gather a small book.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is a funny show; '18' stands for AWFUL, which scrambles NOT into ONT. ONT USES then takes in HEB. The show was a British bus-depot comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1970s British television comedy about a bus driver and his conductor, an example of a sitcom.

clue.text: Air force, European with very loud 18, admitting time's up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means everything is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: 18 down means nasty, and a synonym is awful
T stands for time

explanation.surface: An air force with a deafening, dreadful European admits time has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' stands for a synonym of nasty (18 down). In a down clue 'up' reverses the whole string, which the clue lists in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: The German military flying arm of the Second World War is an air force.

parts.note: 20 down is 'cheers', and 'ta' is British slang for thanks, which cheers also means
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clue made only of numbers referring to other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is a funny show, '20' is the word 'cheers' (thanks, so TA), and 11 is just the number, XI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: An American comedy set in a New York cab company, an example of a sitcom.

clue.text: Funny show featuring model and short groom

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to comb hair is to groom it

explanation.surface: A comedy with a model and a groom who is not tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short groom' looks like a small bridegroom; it is COMB with its end cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a funny TV show built around recurring characters.

clue.text: I think about — without exception — Romeo

parts.note: re means about, concerning
'as one' means all together, without exception
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone muses about Romeo, insisting on no exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what such a person says: someone who reasons might well say 'I think'.
explanation.definitionFit: A logical thinker announces their thought processes, so this is a playful definition by example.

indicators.note: 'after' places the phrase for 'is over' behind the day abbreviation

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
something that is over ends

explanation.surface: Someone announces that something is finished after just a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer at 6 down, a funny show, so the definition is a type of TV comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An American television comedy about six young New Yorkers, an example of a sitcom.

definitions.meaning: to staunch is to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk supporting a leaf or flower

explanation.surface: A loyal backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective meaning loyal; it is the verb meaning stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt bleeding is to check it; a plant's stalk holds it up.

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: 18 down is 'nasty', and a synonym of that is evil
taken as written
U is the old label for socially acceptable (upper-class) usage

explanation.surface: A question about whether something wicked might be a tolerable escape.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' stands for a synonym of the answer at 18 down (nasty), here EVIL; 'retreat' turns EVIL AN U round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without vital signs is lifeless, a modern word for dead.

indicators.note: 'in' puts the party and workers inside the word for 'for'

parts.note: 'for' and 'at' are interchangeable in prices: sold for a pound or at a pound
a bash is an informal party
men are workers, as in a boss and his men

explanation.surface: Party workers attending something for which they feel discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' giving AT is a stretch, as the blogger noted; it works through prices: at five pounds, for five pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment or awkward shame is a kind of discomfort.

clue.text: Anvil's casing of iron — copper's added

indicators.note: the casing of a word is its outside letters, the first and last of iron

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A description of an anvil: an iron shell with copper added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anvil's' reads as 'anvil is'. The anvil here is the tiny bone in the middle ear, not a blacksmith's block.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle-ear bone shaped like a blacksmith's block is called the anvil in plain English.

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the second letter, as in plan B

explanation.surface: Is breaking up a second protest the answer?
explanation.walkthrough: A second protest is 'demo B', like plan B. The definition means disband troops after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge soldiers from service is to disband, or break up, the army units.

clue.text: White vinyl emulsion, no filling required

parts.note: a vinyl is an LP record

indicators.note: emptying out the filling leaves only the outer letters of emulsion

explanation.surface: Instructions for painting: white vinyl emulsion, with no filler needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White vinyl emulsion' reads like paint; 'White' is the egg white.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear part of an egg that turns white when cooked is the egg white.

parts.note: to lack something is to go without it
read as 'one who sums', a summer is an adder

explanation.surface: A comedy about a billionaire missing the summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season: it is someone who adds up. '6' is a funny show, here a British historical comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A British historical comedy starring Rowan Atkinson, an example of a sitcom.

indicators.note: 'after' puts the day letter behind the rearranged word
botched means badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill the day after a cosmetic surgery went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Being troubled by illness or suffering means being sick.

definitions.meaning: 6 down is a funny show: this one was a British comedy set in Chigwell
people who are alike, from 'flock together', and literally flying creatures with plumes

explanation.surface: A comedy show about people who enjoy flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says these 'flock together', so the phrase means similar people; read literally, they fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A British comedy about two Essex women, and an idiom for similar types who flock together.

definitions.meaning: a verb: to coax with compliments
somewhat dull: bland plus the suffix -ish meaning rather

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is more level on its flat face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative adjective; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax with flattery, and, split up, 'rather insipid'.

clue.text: Nasty puncture keeps posh car in the same place

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: a puncture is a hole
RR is short for Rolls-Royce
ib, short for ibidem, means in the same place

explanation.surface: A tyre puncture keeps a luxury car stuck where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posh car' is RR (Rolls-Royce), not U for posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very unpleasant or dreadful is nasty.

clue.text: Bill Clinton's opening line about America results in indictment

indicators.note: 'about' means the bill, opening letter and line go round the country

parts.note: AC is an account, a bill

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's first remark about America leads to his being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Clinton' looks like the president; it is AC (account) and C.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation, a formal charge, is what an indictment is.

clue.text: 6 of clubs, hearts and always spades

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
H is the card abbreviation for hearts
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card hand: some clubs, hearts and plenty of spades.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is a funny show, here a US comedy set in a Boston bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An American comedy set in a Boston bar, an example of a sitcom.

clue.text: Lot of Buddhists prepare to feed the soul

indicators.note: feeding something puts food into it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is the soul
to arm is to prepare for fighting

explanation.surface: Many Buddhists get ready to nourish the spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot' is fate, not a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddhists believe your deeds shape your destiny, your lot in life.

clue.text: A radical actively cuts four in pieces

indicators.note: broken in pieces, the letters are reassembled with some taken away

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A political extremist energetically slashes four people to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' joins 'in pieces' as the signal: the Roman four is taken out and what remains is rearranged. 'radical' is the chemistry term, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit; this one derives from acetic acid.

parts.note: bi is slang for bisexual, swinging both ways
as can mean while: as I walked

explanation.surface: Something swaying while tilting over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency or inclination toward one side is a leaning.

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor
-ess is a suffix marking a female, as in actress

explanation.surface: A bandage handed over by a woman doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind a wound with a covering is to bandage it, used as a verb.

parts.note: so means therefore

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: P stands for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A comedy, therefore pressure starts to be applied.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is a funny show, here a US comedy that parodied daytime dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: An American comedy spoofing daytime dramas, an example of a sitcom.

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: something done cruelly is mangled, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An innocent Greek person was brutally murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person; it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being innocent and trusting is how a young kid behaves.

parts.note: surfing, riding waves, is a watersport
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that out in the open they excel at a watersport.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer says 'great at surfing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer or exterior of anything is its outside.

indicators.note: 'about' puts the reflected word round the word for agony
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: 'Quite!' is an exclamation of agreement, like 'yes'
hell is a state of agony

explanation.surface: A comedy that is rather thoughtful about suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to 6 down: a 1980s British comedy about a grumpy layabout, starring Hywel Bennett.
explanation.definitionFit: A British television comedy series named after its idle hero, an example of a sitcom.
